regions.full_page: HUMILITY FIRST "Learn of me ... meek and humble of heart (Matt. XI 29) "But in all these works let the important warning of the Apostle be carefully remembered: "Neither he that planteth is anything, nor he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase." (I Cor. III 7) PIUS X "Do we think that God is moved by any natural or acquired ex- cellence of ours to use our assistance for the increase of His glory? By no means: for it-written: 'The foolish things of the world hath God chosen that He may confound the wise; and the weak things of the world hath God chosen that He may con- cound the strong and the base things of the world, and the things that are contemptible hath God chosen, and the things that are not, that He might bring to naught things that are'". (I Cor. I. 27-8) "One thing alone joins man with God, makes him pleasing and a not unworthy minister of His mercy; holiness of life and conduct. If this, which is indeed the supereminent knowledge of Jesus Christ, be lacking in a priest, all things are lacking.

"Amen I say to you, whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, shall not enter into it. (Mark X. 15)
